name: Echoveil
description: Echoveil is a mirror-neuron amplifier and oxytocin cascade trigger that dramatically enhances affective empathy — the physical feeling of others' emotional states. At low doses, users experience profound warmth and social attunement; at higher doses, they begin to feel other people's emotions as their own, losing the boundary between self and crowd. It is beloved at intimate gatherings and catastrophically dangerous in crowds.
effects: Intense emotional attunement to nearby individuals
Profound sense of love and connection with others
Physical sensation of others' emotional states
Dissolution of social anxiety and interpersonal barriers
At high doses: crowd-emotion immersion — feeling the aggregate emotional state of groups as a single overwhelming sensation
side_effects: Emotional flooding in large groups or emotionally volatile environments
Identity dissolution at high doses — loss of self-concept
Trauma absorption — taking on others' pain as one's own
Rare: persistent empathic sensitivity that doesn't fully resolve
cultural_context: Echoveil defined the 'Connection Era' of GLMZ party culture in the 2180s and the cultural hangover persists. It's still used at intimate gatherings, grief ceremonies, and certain religious communities as a sacramental tool. The Shelf has its own version — a crude patch called 'Openface' that lacks dose regulation and has caused multiple crowd-panic incidents at underground events. Corporate Tier 4 team-building retreats have been caught using micro-doses in catering without disclosure.
story_hooks: A crowd of 300 Echoveil users at an underground event collectively experienced the same vision during a mass emotional peak — something they describe as a 'presence' — and several have become obsessively focused on recreating the experience

A Tier 4 executive used undisclosed Echoveil micro-dosing at a negotiation session to read emotional states — the opposing party found out and the resulting scandal has escalated into something violent

An Echoveil user at a public execution absorbed the emotional state of the condemned and has not recovered — she remembers dying, and she needs someone to help her understand what she actually experienced
